raw_extraction.description: Twilio provides APIs for communications and messaging, allowing developers to send SMS, voice, and other messages programmatically. It offers RESTful APIs and SDKs to interact with its services.
raw_extraction.api_breadth: Twilio offers a broad set of REST APIs for messaging, voice, and other communication services, with SDKs for multiple programming languages to simplify integration.
raw_extraction.mcp_notes: Twilio provides an official console and developer portal for managing API keys, credentials, and account settings.
raw_extraction.buildability_rationale: Twilio provides comprehensive official documentation with examples for authentication using API keys and Account SID/Auth Token, REST API endpoints, and SDKs in multiple languages, enabling developers to build integrations effectively.

You'll also see examples of how to make requests to the Twilio APIs. Ways to make requests to the Twilio APIs ways-to-make-requests-to-the-twilio-apis page anchor Positive Feedback Negative Feedback You can make an HTTP request to the Twilio API in the following ways: Make a raw HTTP request either in your code (for example, by using a module like got in NodeJS (link takes you to an external page) ) or with a tool like Postman (link takes you to an external page) . Use a Twilio SDK for your preferred programming language. Use the Twilio CLI if you prefer working in the terminal. Authentication authentication page anchor Positive Feedback Negative Feedback (information) Environment variables Always store your credentials in environment variables before sharing any code or deploying to production. Learn more about setting environment variables (link takes you to an external page) . To authenticate requests to the Twilio APIs, use HTTP Basic authentication (link takes you to an external page) . Use your API key SID as the username and your API key secret as the password. (information) Regional API credentials Twilio API credentials are region-specific resources. If your account uses Twilio Regions , see Manage Regional API credentials . Use API keys use-api-keys page anchor Positive Feedback Negative Feedback An API key is a unique identifier that allows a client to access your Twilio account and create, read, update, or delete resources through the Twilio APIs. You can create multiple API keys for different purposes, such as for different developers or subsystems within your application. If a key is compromised or no longer used, you can revoke it to prevent unauthorized access. Use API keys for your applications unless the API reference or guide specifies Account SID and Auth Token authentication . If a key is compromised or no longer used, revoke it to prevent unauthorized access without affecting your other applications. You can create an API key either in the Twilio Console or using the API . The API key types are Main , Standard , and Restricted (Key resource v1 only). The following table describes each type: Key type Access permissions Create in Console Create with REST API Main Full access to all Twilio API resources. Equivalent to using your Account SID and Auth Token for API requests. Yes No Standard Access to all Twilio API resources, except for Accounts ( /Accounts ) or Keys ( /Accounts/{SID}/Keys , /v1/Keys ) resources. Yes Yes Restricted Customized, fine-grained access to specific Twilio API resources. Learn more about Restricted API keys . Yes Yes ( v1 only ) When making an API request, use your API key as the username and your API key secret as the password. Note : In the following example, you must use a Main API key. List accounts Link to code sample: List accounts curl Report code block Copy code block 1 curl -X GET "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts.json?PageSize=20" \ 2 -u $TWILIO_API_KEY : $TWILIO_API_SECRET The user remains logged in for the duration of the request. Learn more about how Twilio handles authentication . Use your Account SID and Auth Token using-your-account-sid-and-auth-token page anchor Positive Feedback Negative Feedback When an API reference or guide specifies Account SID and Auth Token authentication, use the Account SID as the HTTP Basic authentication username and the Auth Token as the password. Store these values in the TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN environment variables. Follow the credential requirements for the operation you're performing: Accounts examples use Account SID and Auth Token authentication. For subaccount management , use the parent account's credentials. Main API keys are an alternative, but Standard API keys can't access Accounts resources. Auth Token promotion and Secondary Auth Token examples use Account SID and Auth Token authentication for token rotation. Test credential examples use your test Account SID and test Auth Token, not your live credentials or an API key. Guides such as A2P 10DLC onboarding for ISVs and the BrandRegistrations API reference specify which account's credentials to use. Don't substitute parent account credentials for subaccount credentials unless the guide supports that operation. For example, the following request lists accounts using Account SID and Auth Token authentication: List accounts with an Auth Token Link to code sample: List accounts with an Auth Token curl Report code block Copy code block 1 curl -X GET "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts.json?PageSize=20" \ 2 -u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID : $TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN Twilio SDKs twilio-sdks page anchor Positive Feedback Negative Feedback A Twilio SDK is a server-side SDK that helps you use Twilio's REST APIs, generate TwiML, and perform other common server-side programming tasks. Twilio SDKs can handle credential management and simplify the authentication process. All Twilio SDKs come with a Utilities class that validates requests by passing your credentials to the library. HTTP methods for API interactions http-methods-for-api-interactions page anchor Positive Feedback Negative Feedback Twilio APIs use standard RESTful HTTP methods to perform actions on resources. The following examples demonstrate the most common methods: POST : Create or update a resource. GET : Retrieve a resource. DELETE : Delete a resource.
